notes: Identity independently checked: title Not Pollyannas: Higher Generalized Trust Predicts Lie Detection Ability; Nancy L. Carter and J. Mark Weber; DOI 10.1177/1948550609360261; Social Psychological and Personality Science 1(3), 274–279, 2010. Supplied canonical text is a six-page primary research report with methods, results, discussion, appendices and references, rather than an abstract or secondary article. No PDF was supplied, so no rendering performed. Assigned original fields only; replication and reported_success are unassigned placeholders. Target ambiguity: supplied p.4 corresponds to printed p.277, General Discussion, without the focal accuracy coefficients; the preceding results (printed p.276) distinguish multiple outcomes. Printed candidates: overall accuracy r=.529, p=.003 (equal); lie-only accuracy r=.536, p=.003 (equal); truth-only accuracy r=.12, p=.537 (equal); sensitivity to deceit F(1,27)=8.44, p=.007 (equal), R2=.24. These are separate tests; no metric conversions performed. The broad deception detection description does not uniquely select overall versus lie-only accuracy. Candidate N=29 is explicitly a recruitment count, with r(29) printed for correlations; it is not promoted to analytic N or derived from degrees of freedom. Eight stimuli comprise four lie and four truth videos, not mutually exclusive participant groups. No N sum performed. All assigned values remain null with confidence false pending target clarification; candidates preserved for field-scope review.
